title: The gourd and the saved city
word: The gourd and the saved city
hook: Yunus is cast ashore, sick, and shaded by a gourd vine, and the people he walked away from turn back and are spared
tomorrow: Mecca, a valley of trade and idols

segments.voice: Yesterday, three darknesses, and Yunus's prayer from inside the fish. Your line was la ilaha illa anta: there is no god but You. Did you say it anywhere dark? Day seventy-seven, the end of week eleven.

The Qur'an tells it in a single line: Allah cast him on a bare shore while he was sick. That's all it says. A man lying on the sand under a hard sun, weak, barely able to lift his head. No shade, no food, no one. The man who walked out on his people has nothing left at all. And then, right over him, something begins to grow. A vine, with wide green leaves, spreading over his body like an umbrella. The Qur'an names the plant. It's a gourd.
screen: `A BARE SHORE, A SICK MAN.` → `NO SHADE, NO ONE.` → `A VINE BEGINS TO GROW.`

segments.voice: Here's the line in Pickthall's translation: “And We caused a tree of gourd to grow above him.” In Arabic, yaqtin. Commentators explain it as a fast-growing gourd with broad leaves, the kind that gives quick shade and keeps flies away from a sick man's skin. A small mercy, exactly sized to what he needed. Then the Qur'an turns to the part of the story Yunus never saw coming: “And We sent him to a hundred thousand (folk) or more.” And they believed. The people he walked out on. The ones he was sure would never listen. They turned back to Allah. Surah Yunus, the tenth surah, the one named for him, singles them out. It wishes aloud that the other towns warned of old had believed in time, as the people of Yunus did. When they believed, the punishment was lifted from them, and they were given enjoyment of life for a while. Here's the shape of it. Yunus left because he was certain they wouldn't change. And they changed. Commentators say the people went out together, men, women and children, and cried to Allah when they saw the warning signs, and they were spared. In the Qur'an's stories of warned towns, this is the one the text holds up as turning around in time. And that closes week eleven: a messenger in the eastern place, a palm tree, a baby who spoke, Isa by Allah's leave, a man who left in anger, three darknesses, and a gourd vine over a city that believed.
screen: `A TREE OF GOURD ABOVE HIM.` · `A HUNDRED THOUSAND OR MORE.` · `THE TOWN THAT TURNED IN TIME.` · `HE WAS SURE. THEY CHANGED.` · then, large: `THE CITY BELIEVED.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: go back to one thing you left. Settle, and breathe. Think of something you walked away from, or someone you gave up on, a friendship, a project, a skill, a relative. Maybe you were sure it would never change. Just picture it now, today, without the old certainty. What if it has changed? What if you have? Choose one small step back toward it: a text, an email, ten minutes. If you pray, you can ask Allah to open the way. The bell holds the time.
The gourd and the saved city. A vine shades a sick prophet on the shore, and the people he gave up on turn back and are spared.
screen: `THE GOURD AND THE SAVED CITY — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: the city believed. Today, take the one small step back toward what you left. Eleven weeks on the path. Tomorrow, the stories of the prophets arrive in a valley called Mecca. Day seventy-seven.

screen: `DAY 77 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: MECCA, A VALLEY OF TRADE AND IDOLS.`

howItsDone: Muslims read the end of Yunus's story in Surah As-Saffat and Surah Yunus, and it is often recalled as a reminder that no one should despair of a people turning back to Allah.

fork.setup: Yunus lies on the shore, sick, under a gourd vine. the people he walked out on, the ones he was sure would never change: what happened to them?
fork.reveal: they believed, a hundred thousand or more, and were given enjoyment of life for a while (37:147–148; 10:98).

trapdoor: what you thought: a man survives a whale.
what it means: the prophet who gave up on his people is shaded and healed, and the people he gave up on turn back.
what a scholar hears: 10:98 singles out qawm Yunus, the people of Yunus, as the one town that believed in time and was spared, the reverse of the other warned towns in the Qur'an.

sources.ref: Qur'an 37:145, 37:148 (cast on a bare shore, sick; they believed)
Qur'an 10:98 (the people of Yunus believed and were spared)
Tafsir Ibn Kathir on 37:146 and 10:98 (the gourd; the people going out together)

notes: Pickthall 37:146 and 37:147 quoted from memory; confirm exact wording.
Order of events: many commentators say the people believed while Yunus was gone, and he returned to them after the shore; the script keeps that ambiguity ('the part Yunus never saw coming'). Confirm.
The gourd's properties (quick shade, keeps flies away) are from tafsir, stated as 'commentators explain'. Confirm.
'The only whole city ... that turned around in time' paraphrases the usual reading of 10:98; confirm.
